01

Setting specification

Task

Return an approximate solution of the symmetric positive-definite linear system. Accuracy is measured by the stated normalized energy error.

Solve $Ax=b$, whose unique solution is $x^\star=A^{-1}b$.

Admissible model

The matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ is symmetric positive definite, $d\ge1$, and its spectral condition number is $\lambda_{\max}(A)/\lambda_{\min}(A)\le\kappa$, where $\kappa\ge1$. No absolute spectral scale, sparsity, or preconditioner is promised.

Oracle interface

Inputs $d,\kappa,\varepsilon,b,x_0$ are public, with $b,x_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$; $A$ is hidden. Any $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$ may be queried for exact $Av$. All responses use one fixed matrix; repetitions are not independent samples.

Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and the complete matrix are not free interfaces.

Output

Return any $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d$, including an unqueried point or any postprocessing of the transcript. No additional error certificate is required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

The energy norm is $\|z\|_A^2=z^{\mathsf T}Az$. If $x_0\ne x^\star$, the base loss is $\ell(\widehat{x})=\|\widehat{x}-x^\star\|_A^2/(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|x_0-x^\star\|_2^2)$ and must satisfy $\ell\le\varepsilon$.

If $x_0=x^\star$, success requires $\widehat x=x^\star$. The criterion is neither relative initial energy error nor relative residual.

Resource accounting

Count right products with single vectors only: $N=N_{\mathrm r}$. A block of width $q$ costs $q$ calls.

The budget bounds calls for every fixed input and every private seed. Reading public inputs, exact real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are free. One call applies the interface to one vector.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Algorithms may use private randomness and choose query vectors adaptively from the declared domain using all previous responses. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript; no Krylov or linear-span restriction applies. Exact internal arithmetic, storage, and communication are free in this oracle model. A block query is charged by its number of columns.

The algorithm is selected using only public inputs. For every admissible input fixed before its private seed is generated, the success event has probability at least $2/3$ over that private randomness.

Budget convention
A fixed worst-case budget respected for every input and private seed.

B4

General randomized adaptive queries; randomly rotated spectral families and polynomial-approximation lower bounds

The matrix-vector complexity of Ax = b ↗
Algorithm scope
Both deterministic algorithms and algorithms with private randomness are permitted. Queries may depend on the entire response history. Query vectors are unrestricted; no Krylov, span, or zero-respecting condition is imposed. Storage, exact-real computation, and communication have no additional constraints. Parallel block calls are still charged by column.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants
Positive universal constants, permitted to depend on any explicitly fixed auxiliary parameters.
Derivation
Fix the auxiliary parameters in the source Theorem E.2 at $\delta_0=\eta_0=1/2$. Its sufficient dimension condition is $d\ge C\kappa^{13}$, its residual threshold is $1/d$, and its required success probability is $5/6$. Choose the hard-instance initial point $x_0=0$. Let $e_x=\widehat x-x^\star$, $\beta_A=\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, and $\mu_A=\lambda_{\min}(A)$. Then $$\|Ae_x\|_2^2\le\beta_A\|e_x\|_A^2\le\varepsilon\beta_A^2\|x^\star\|_2^2,\qquad \|b\|_2\ge\mu_A\|x^\star\|_2,$$ so the relative residual on success is at most $\kappa\sqrt\varepsilon$. The condition $\varepsilon\le\kappa^{-2}d^{-2}$ ensures the source residual threshold. Run a $2/3$-success algorithm independently three times, spend one additional $A\widehat x$ query per output, and select the smallest residual. At least one run succeeds with probability $1-(1/3)^3=26/27>5/6$. If the original budget is $N$, the source theorem excludes $3(N+1)<c\sqrt\kappa\log d$, giving $N\ge c'\sqrt\kappa\log d-O(1)$. On the strip $d^{-4}\le\varepsilon\le\kappa^{-2}d^{-2}$, we have $\log(1/\varepsilon)=\Theta(\log d)$, while $d\ge C\kappa^{13}$ ensures that the reconstruction branch does not change the order. Thus deterministic CG and the unrestricted randomized lower bound match up to constants in this strip; this does not establish optimality for every $(d,\kappa,\varepsilon)$.
Upper bound
\[O(\sqrt\kappa\log d)\]
B1

Deterministic conjugate gradient, charged by actual $Av$ calls
